title: Training and Model Optimization
description: Understand loss functions, optimization, regularization, and training diagnostics.

questions.prompt: In model training, what does an objective function usually quantify?
options: A scalar criterion the optimizer seeks to minimize or maximize
questions.explanation: An objective combines a data-fit term and possibly regularization to define what training optimizes.

questions.prompt: What is a mini-batch gradient estimate computed from?
questions.explanation: Mini-batch training estimates a gradient from a subset, reducing computation per update while introducing sampling noise.

questions.prompt: A learning rate that is too large can make optimization unstable or divergent.
questions.explanation: Oversized steps may overshoot low-loss regions and cause loss oscillation or growth.

questions.prompt: What is the common purpose of momentum in gradient optimization?
options: Accumulate a smoothed direction from past gradients
Normalize input features to unit variance
questions.explanation: Momentum smooths updates using a running velocity, often accelerating progress along consistent directions.

questions.prompt: What distinguishes Adam from plain stochastic gradient descent?
options: It adapts per-parameter step sizes using moving gradient statistics
questions.explanation: Adam tracks moving averages of gradients and squared gradients to adapt updates by parameter.

questions.prompt: Which statements about weight decay are accurate?
options: It can discourage overly complex fits
It is often related to L2 regularization
questions.explanation: Weight decay discourages large weights and can regularize a model; it does not alter labels.

questions.prompt: What is a typical early-stopping signal?
options: The test set contains an even number of rows
questions.explanation: Early stopping halts when validation performance plateaus or worsens, limiting over-training.

questions.prompt: Standard dropout randomly disables units during ordinary inference.
questions.explanation: Dropout is generally disabled at inference; implementations maintain expected activation magnitude.

questions.prompt: What is one common trade-off of using a larger training batch?
options: More examples per gradient estimate but potentially more memory use
questions.explanation: Larger batches can produce smoother estimates while requiring more memory and potentially changing optimization behavior.

questions.prompt: Why might training use gradient clipping?
questions.explanation: Clipping constrains gradient magnitude and can stabilize training when gradients become unusually large.

questions.prompt: Which pairings are commonly appropriate?
options: Mean squared error for continuous regression
Accuracy as a differentiable gradient objective by default
questions.explanation: MSE, cross-entropy, and hinge loss are common objectives. Accuracy is usually nondifferentiable and not directly optimized.

questions.prompt: The metric used to select a deployed model must always be identical to its differentiable training loss.
questions.explanation: Training loss enables optimization; model selection can instead use application-relevant metrics.

questions.prompt: What is a characteristic effect associated with L1 regularization?
options: It can drive some coefficients exactly to zero
It removes the intercept by definition
questions.explanation: The absolute-value penalty can yield sparse coefficient estimates, effectively selecting features in some settings.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of a learning-rate schedule?
options: Change the step size over the course of training
Change the target labels every epoch
Convert a classifier into a regressor
questions.explanation: Schedules adjust optimization steps over time, often using smaller steps later in training.

questions.prompt: Which observations can indicate a training problem?
options: Validation loss rises while training loss falls
A model file has a descriptive name
questions.explanation: NaN loss and persistent oscillation may indicate unstable updates; diverging validation loss can signal overfitting.

questions.prompt: Why is careful parameter initialization useful in deep models?
options: It can help keep activations and gradients in workable ranges
It selects the test metric automatically
It removes the need for data
questions.explanation: Initialization affects signal propagation and optimization; suitable schemes reduce vanishing or exploding activations.

questions.prompt: Freezing a parameter means its value is not updated by the optimizer.
questions.explanation: Frozen parameters are excluded from gradient-based updates, though they can still participate in forward computation.

questions.prompt: Which is a hyperparameter rather than a parameter learned directly from training examples?
questions.explanation: The learning rate is configured to control optimization; model parameters are adjusted from data.

questions.prompt: What does a zero gradient at a point establish?
options: The first-order local slope is zero there
The point is necessarily a global minimum
The model has no training data
questions.explanation: A zero gradient identifies a stationary point, which may be a minimum, maximum, or saddle point.

questions.prompt: Which steps can improve reproducibility of model experiments?
options: Set and record random seeds where applicable
Report only the best run without selection details
questions.explanation: Versioning, seeds, and logs aid repeatability; selective reporting hides variability and selection effects.
